summary: This sermon explores the theological significance of Christ's ascension, distinguishing it from resurrection and emphasizing that only God can cause someone to ascend to heaven. The speaker argues that the ascension is an overlooked but vital doctrine that enabled the Holy Spirit to come to all believers and made Jesus the ongoing mediator between heaven and earth.
key_points: Ascension differs from resurrection: only God can cause ascension, not human effort
Old Testament foreshadowing through Elijah's ascent and Moses' mountain encounters
Jesus' ascension was necessary for the Holy Spirit to come to all believers
Heaven and earth converge in Jesus, who remains active as mediator at God's right hand
The call to witness extends geographically and temporally to the ends of the earth and end of time
big_idea: Jesus had to ascend to the Father's right hand so the Holy Spirit could be sent to empower all believers as witnesses of the gospel everywhere until the end of time.
title: Resurrection Rumors: The Ascension Encounter
